chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār narrated from al-Ḥusayn [al-Ḥusayn, variant reading] ibn Saʿīd, from al-Ḥārith ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Aḥwal, the companion of al-Ṭāq, from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Ṣādiq, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: "Whoever loves to be the most honored of people, then let him have taqwa of Allah. Whoever loves to be the most God-conscious of people, then let him place his trust in Allah, the Exalted. And whoever loves to be the richest of people, then let him be more trusting of what is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than of what is in his own hand."

Then he عليه السلام said: "Shall I inform you of the worst of people?" They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "The one who hates people and is hated by people." Then he said: "Shall I inform you of one worse than that?" They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "The one who does not excuse a slip, does not accept an apology, and does not forgive a sin." Then he said: "Shall I inform you of one worse than that?"

They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "The one from whose evil one is not safe and whose good is not hoped for. Indeed, ʿĪsā ibn Maryam عليه السلام stood among Banī Isrāʾīl and said: O Banī Isrāʾīl, do not speak wisdom to the ignorant, lest you wrong it; and do not withhold it from its people, lest you wrong them. And do not aid the oppressor in his oppression, lest your merit be nullified. Matters are three: a matter whose right guidance has become clear to you, so follow it; and a matter whose error has become clear to you, so avoid it; and a matter about which there is disagreement, so refer it to Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

key_terms.الظَّالِمَ: the oppressor; one whose wrongdoing must not be supported
key_terms.بِالْحِكْمَةِ: wisdom; knowledge that must be given appropriately
key_terms.بِمَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: what is with Allah; divine provision and reward as the real source of richness
key_terms.عَثْرَةً: a slip or lapse for which one should excuse others
key_terms.فَرُدَّهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: refer it back to Allah; returning disputed matters to divine authority
key_terms.فَلْيَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ: let him place his trust in Allah; the mark of true piety
key_terms.فَلْيَتَّقِ اللَّهَ: let him have taqwa of Allah; the basis of true honor
key_terms.مَعْذِرَةً: an apology or excuse that should be accepted

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe true honor, piety, wealth, and the worst kinds of people?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that true honor, taqwa, and richness come through fearing Allah, trusting Him, and relying on what is with Him over worldly possession. It also warns against harshness toward people, refusing excuses, and becoming a person whose harm is feared and whose good is not expected, while affirming the proper transmission of wisdom and referring disputed matters back to Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5858 - Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Numan Al-Ahwal, known as Sahib Al-Taq, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said that the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said:

"Whoever wishes to be the most honored among people should fear Allah (swt).
Whoever wishes to be the most pious among people should place his trust in Allah (swt), the Exalted.
And whoever wishes to be the richest among people should have more trust in what is with Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, than in what is in his own hands."

Then Prophet (sw), peace be upon him, said: "Shall I inform you of the worst of people?"
They replied: "Yes, O' Messenger of Allah (swt)."
Prophet (sw) said: "The one who hates people and whom people hate."
Then Prophet (sw) said: "Shall I inform you of someone worse than that?"
They said: "Yes, O' Messenger of Allah (swt)."
Prophet (sw) said: "The one who does not forgive a slip, does not accept an excuse, and does not pardon a sin."
Then Prophet (sw) said: "Shall I inform you of someone even worse than that?"
They said: "Yes, O' Messenger of Allah (swt)."

Prophet (sw) said: "The one whose harm is not safe from and whose goodness is not hoped for.
Indeed, Isa (Jesus) (as), the son of Mary {s.a}, peace be upon him, stood among the Children of Israel and said: 'O' Children of Israel, do not speak wisdom to the ignorant lest you wrong it, and do not withhold it from its rightful people lest you wrong them.
Do not support the oppressor in his oppression, or your virtue will be nullified.
Matters are of three kinds:
A matter whose guidance is clear to you, so follow it.
A matter whose misguidance is clear to you, so avoid it.
And a matter in which there is disagreement, so refer it back to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic.'"
